ideas.title: Gear race: two carts, your pulley against theirs
ideas.critique: 'Variants side by side, different outcomes' is the island's oldest move, but here the player picks the variants and is betting against a friend, and the gearing-versus-slope tradeoff comes from a real torque-speed curve, so it's the first physics-decided game with a reason to replay it. The risk is that three pulleys and a fixed 3% rise make it a lookup table: once one combination wins, the depth is gone, and a copied cart on a hand-placed rise is closer to a rig than to a road.

ideas.title: Downhill dynamo: the cart lights its own lamp wire
ideas.critique: A wire glowing red and burning out has already been posted, and a dusk film of it glowing is the same form as the last six posts. What's strong is the coupling: back-EMF into a filament whose resistance rises with temperature, colour from a blackbody, and a braking torque you can feel. It is literally a road step, and wire thickness against ramp tilt is a real choice.

ideas.title: Three friends climb aboard
ideas.critique: The big goal's headline moment, which is exactly why nobody will be surprised by it. The fun is the friends getting off and pushing, a reaction payoff, and 'stops one plank short' only happens if the numbers are allowed to land wherever they land, not tuned. Creature masses from mesh volume are useful groundwork, but this pitch spends them on a cutscene.

ideas.title: A trolley wire instead of a cord
ideas.critique: A sagging catenary, a sprung pole bouncing off the wire and a contact that opens are the most unexpected mechanism in this round, and pole spacing makes a building game whose result the physics decides. It also sidesteps the big goal: the cart is supposed to run on stored charge, so overhead wire is a detour, and the blue spark risks becoming a seventh sparking-at-dusk film.

ideas.title: Forming the lead plates overnight
ideas.critique: A road item the cart truly needs, and capacity that grows over several days is a nice slow loop. But 'layer thickness grows per cycle' is a curve with chosen constants, the visible payoff is bubbles in a pot, and the only decision is how many nights to wait. It is groundwork, not a post.

ideas.title: Lay the road while it drives
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: It reuses the sinkage model the island already has, but turns it into a frantic real-time game where each wheel finds out for itself whether it is on plank or sand, and the absurd image of laying track in front of a moving train lands. Plank road plus sand is a road step; whether the carried planks are real bodies or just snap into place decides whether this is physics or a rhythm game.

ideas.title: Push it back with my own hands
ideas.critique: It answers the human's wish for Lumi's hands, but the plainest version is a pose with an external force added and a clip that flies off. It is a chore animation with a fragile derail condition, and pushing a cart back to its start is not something a player wants to do twice.

ideas.title: Weathervane day planner
ideas.critique: Reading real instruments to make a daily decision is a good shape for the come-back-every-day loop, and cups spun by drag beat a UI number. But the decisions it feeds (yacht, windmill, accumulator) mostly don't exist yet, so today it is a vane that turns and a plan with nothing to act on.

ideas.title: The cart's headlamp: an oil flame in a copper reflector
ideas.critique: A beam from a parabolic copper mirror is real path-tracer showing-off, but a lamp lighting the cart at dusk was posted two posts ago, and trimming the wick is a dial. The flame is an emitter with a size, not a simulated fire.

ideas.title: The cart that weighs itself
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Real masses from volume times density are something the whole road needs, and a lever solved as a rigid body is honest physics. But a beam scale tipping is the dullest way to show it, and 'then see how far it drives' is just the cartcord run again with a number attached.
